"""Per-session turn lease — serializes the [load history -> run -> flush] region.

Busy guards are keyed by ROUTING KEY but the transcript is owned by SESSION_ID, and
``switch_session()`` makes key->id many-to-one (/resume from a second chat, CLI-continuity,
delegation pinning, topic tip-walks), so two keys could interleave flushes on one transcript
(``user;user`` wedge). The lease serializes per RESOLVED session_id: acquired right before the
transcript load, released in the dispatch layer's ``finally``; identity-checked release; a
timed-out waiter fails CLOSED (:class:`TurnLeaseTimeoutError`); only idle entries evict. Limits:
CLI-continuity processes are outside this lock; mid-turn rotation alias is closed by ``rebind``.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import time
from typing import Dict, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Cap on tracked leases. Idle entries evict oldest-first; live leases never do, so a burst of
# distinct sessions may transiently exceed the cap rather than break serialization.
DEFAULT_MAX_LEASES = 512
# Fallback wait (seconds) when the caller passes no positive timeout (bridged via
# HERMES_TURN_LEASE_TIMEOUT — lease contention is not agent inactivity). Fail-closed but short:
# never pin a sequential platform updater for minutes.
DEFAULT_LEASE_WAIT = 5.0


def _holder_desc(holder: Optional["TurnLeaseToken"]) -> tuple:
    return (holder.owner_key, holder.generation) if holder else ("?", "?")


class TurnLeaseTimeoutError(TimeoutError):
    """Lease held for the full wait budget; fail-closed: caller must not enter the turn region."""

    def __init__(self, session_id: str, *, owner_key: str, generation: int, wait_seconds: float):
        self.session_id, self.owner_key = session_id, owner_key
        self.generation, self.wait_seconds = generation, wait_seconds
        super().__init__(f"turn lease wait timed out after {wait_seconds:.0f}s on session "
                         f"{session_id} for routing key {owner_key} (gen {generation})")


class TurnLeaseToken:
    """Held-lease handle from :meth:`SessionTurnLeaseRegistry.acquire`; ``released`` makes
    release idempotent."""

    __slots__ = ("session_id", "owner_key", "generation", "released", "lease")

    def __init__(self, session_id: str, owner_key: str, generation: int, lease: "_SessionLease") -> None:
        self.session_id, self.owner_key, self.generation = session_id, owner_key, generation
        self.released = False
        # The concrete lease, so release resolves by identity even after a rotation re-aliases
        # ``session_id`` (both ids map to this same lease).
        self.lease = lease

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug aid
        return (f"TurnLeaseToken(session_id={self.session_id!r}, owner_key={self.owner_key!r}, "
                f"generation={self.generation}, released={self.released})")


class _SessionLease:
    __slots__ = ("lock", "holder", "acquired_at", "last_used", "pending_acquires")

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self.holder: Optional[TurnLeaseToken] = None
        self.acquired_at, self.last_used, self.pending_acquires = 0.0, time.time(), 0

    @property
    def idle(self) -> bool:
        """True when evictable: nobody holds or awaits it."""
        return self.holder is None and not self.lock.locked() and self.pending_acquires == 0


class SessionTurnLeaseRegistry:
    """Asyncio lease per resolved session_id. Process-local, single-event-loop by design (same
    visibility scope as the routing-key guards it extends); call only from the gateway loop."""

    def __init__(self, max_entries: int = DEFAULT_MAX_LEASES) -> None:
        self._leases: Dict[str, _SessionLease] = {}
        self._max_entries = max(1, int(max_entries))

    def _get_or_create(self, session_id: str) -> _SessionLease:
        if (lease := self._leases.get(session_id)) is None:
            self._evict_idle()
            lease = self._leases[session_id] = _SessionLease()
        lease.last_used = time.time()
        return lease

    def _evict_idle(self) -> None:
        """Drop oldest idle entries to fit a new lease under the cap; never a held/contended one."""
        if (overflow := len(self._leases) - self._max_entries + 1) <= 0:
            return
        idle = sorted((sid for sid, l in self._leases.items() if l.idle),
                      key=lambda sid: self._leases[sid].last_used)
        for sid in idle[:overflow]:
            self._leases.pop(sid, None)

    async def acquire(
        self, session_id: str, *, owner_key: str, generation: int, timeout: Optional[float] = None
    ) -> Optional[TurnLeaseToken]:
        """Acquire the lease for ``session_id``, waiting if held. Raises
        :class:`TurnLeaseTimeoutError` when the wait budget expires; None for a falsy id."""
        if not session_id:
            return None
        wait = float(timeout) if timeout and timeout > 0 else DEFAULT_LEASE_WAIT
        lease = self._get_or_create(session_id)
        token = TurnLeaseToken(session_id, owner_key, int(generation), lease=lease)
        if lease.lock.locked():
            logger.warning(
                "turn lease contention on session %s: routing key %s (gen %s) waiting behind "
                "in-flight turn held by routing key %s (gen %s, held %.0fs) — two routing keys "
                "are mapped to one session_id (#64934); serializing this turn behind the previous "
                "turn's flush",
                session_id, owner_key, generation, *_holder_desc(lease.holder),
                time.time() - lease.acquired_at if lease.acquired_at else -1.0)
        # Lock.release() wakes a waiter while leaving the lock momentarily unlocked. Count every
        # in-progress acquire across that handoff (even apparently-uncontended ones — wait_for()
        # may schedule them before the lock coroutine runs) so eviction cannot orphan the old
        # lock and create a second lock for the same session.
        lease.pending_acquires += 1
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(lease.lock.acquire(), timeout=wait)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            logger.error(
                "turn lease wait timed out after %.0fs on session %s (waiter: routing key %s gen "
                "%s; holder: routing key %s gen %s) — failing closed: refusing to run this turn "
                "UNSERIALIZED against the still-held lease",
                wait, session_id, owner_key, generation, *_holder_desc(lease.holder))
            raise TurnLeaseTimeoutError(
                session_id, owner_key=owner_key, generation=generation, wait_seconds=wait) from None
        finally:
            lease.pending_acquires -= 1
        # Lock held and no await before holder publication, so the lease cannot become
        # evictable after the pending count is cleared.
        lease.holder = token
        lease.acquired_at = lease.last_used = time.time()
        return token

    def rebind(self, token: Optional[TurnLeaseToken], new_session_id: str) -> bool:
        """Alias a HELD lease onto ``new_session_id`` after mid-turn rotation (compression) so the
        flush target stays serialized: the SAME ``_SessionLease`` is registered under the new id
        (old mapping idle-evicts later), only the holder may rebind, the token follows. A live
        lease on the new id: log loudly, keep the old id (fail-open)."""
        if (token is None or token.released or not new_session_id
                or new_session_id == token.session_id):
            return False
        lease = token.lease
        if lease.holder is not token:
            return False
        existing = self._leases.get(new_session_id)
        if existing is not None and existing is not lease and not existing.idle:
            logger.warning(
                "turn lease rebind blocked: session %s rotated to %s mid-turn (holder: routing key "
                "%s gen %s) but the target session's lease is already live (holder: routing key %s "
                "gen %s) — keeping the lease on the old id; transcript writes on %s may "
                "interleave (#64934 rotation-alias edge)",
                token.session_id, new_session_id, token.owner_key, token.generation,
                *_holder_desc(existing.holder), new_session_id)
            return False
        self._leases[new_session_id] = lease
        lease.last_used = time.time()
        token.session_id = new_session_id
        return True

    def release(self, token: Optional[TurnLeaseToken]) -> bool:
        """Release ``token``'s lease. Idempotent; True only when this exact token was the current
        holder (a re-release or a stale token whose slot went to a newer turn is a safe no-op)."""
        if token is None or token.released:
            return False
        token.released = True
        lease = token.lease
        if lease.holder is not token:
            logger.debug("turn lease release skipped on session %s: token (key %s gen %s) is not "
                         "the current holder", token.session_id, token.owner_key, token.generation)
            return False
        lease.holder, lease.acquired_at, lease.last_used = None, 0.0, time.time()
        if lease.lock.locked():
            lease.lock.release()
        return True
"""Behavior tests for the per-session turn lease (#64934).

The lease serializes the [load history → run → flush] region per RESOLVED
session_id, closing the alias-key overlap route: two routing keys mapped to
one session_id via switch_session() run turns on two different agent objects,
invisible to every routing-key guard.

Covers:
- alias-key turn waits until the first turn's flush, and flush order is
  preserved (the second turn loads history AFTER the first turn's release)
- distinct sessions do not contend
- generation-scoped, idempotent release: a stale unwind can never free a
  newer turn's lease; double-release is a no-op
- timeout fail-closed: a timed-out waiter never enters the transcript region,
  and outer dispatch returns a visible rejection/resend notice without invoking
  goal continuation
- registry stays bounded; live and pending leases are never evicted
- timed-out and cancelled acquire attempts do not pin idle registry entries
- GatewayRunner._release_turn_lease wiring (bare-runner safe, token-scoped)
"""

import asyncio
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock

import pytest

from gateway.turn_lease import (
    SessionTurnLeaseRegistry,
    TurnLeaseTimeoutError,
)


def _run(coro):
    return asyncio.run(coro)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serialization behavior
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_alias_key_turn_waits_and_order_is_preserved():
    """Second routing key on the same session_id waits for the first turn's
    release; events interleave in strict [load1, flush1, load2, flush2] order."""

    async def scenario():
        registry = SessionTurnLeaseRegistry()
        events = []

        async def turn(owner_key, generation, hold):
            token = await registry.acquire(
                "sess-1", owner_key=owner_key, generation=generation, timeout=5
            )
            assert token is not None
            events.append(f"load:{owner_key}")
            await asyncio.sleep(hold)  # simulate run + flush
            events.append(f"flush:{owner_key}")
            registry.release(token)

        t1 = asyncio.create_task(turn("key-a", 1, hold=0.05))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)  # let turn 1 take the lease
        t2 = asyncio.create_task(turn("key-b", 1, hold=0))
        await asyncio.gather(t1, t2)
        return events

    events = _run(scenario())
    assert events == ["load:key-a", "flush:key-a", "load:key-b", "flush:key-b"]


def test_distinct_sessions_do_not_contend():
    async def scenario():
        registry = SessionTurnLeaseRegistry()
        order = []

        async def turn(session_id, owner_key):
            token = await registry.acquire(
                session_id, owner_key=owner_key, generation=1, timeout=5
            )
            order.append(f"start:{session_id}")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
            order.append(f"end:{session_id}")
            registry.release(token)

        await asyncio.gather(turn("sess-a", "key-a"), turn("sess-b", "key-b"))
        return order

    order = _run(scenario())
    # Both started before either finished — no serialization across sessions.
    assert order[:2] == ["start:sess-a", "start:sess-b"]

def test_timeout_fails_closed_instead_of_authorizing_an_unserialized_turn():
    """A timed-out waiter must never run against the still-live holder.

    Returning a degraded token used to authorize exactly that unsafe path.
    The two turns could then load the same history base and interleave their
    transcript writes, defeating the serialization invariant this lease owns.
    """

    async def scenario():
        registry = SessionTurnLeaseRegistry()
        holder = await registry.acquire(
            "sess-timeout", owner_key="key-a", generation=1, timeout=1
        )
        assert holder is not None

        with pytest.raises(TurnLeaseTimeoutError):
            await registry.acquire(
                "sess-timeout", owner_key="key-b", generation=1, timeout=0.02
            )

        # The timeout neither steals nor releases the live holder's lease.
        assert registry._leases["sess-timeout"].holder is holder
        assert registry.release(holder) is True

        # Once the holder releases, a later turn can acquire normally.
        successor = await registry.acquire(
            "sess-timeout", owner_key="key-b", generation=2, timeout=1
        )
        assert successor is not None
        assert registry.release(successor) is True

    _run(scenario())

    """Credential-scrubbed env for an agent-browser subprocess (deferred import: test
    harnesses stub the ``tools`` package). The passthrough keys are re-added from the active
    profile's secret scope, never ``os.environ``: under multiplex that holds the LAUNCH profile's
    Browserbase/Firecrawl keys, and a served profile's browser must run on its own (or none)."""
    from agent.secret_scope import current_secret_scope, get_secret, serves_routed_profile
    from tools.environments.local import served_profile_child_env

    # A routed profile (multiplex, or a Desktop/dashboard backend serving ``?profile=B`` with the

"""Per-session turn lease — serializes the [load history -> run -> flush] region.

Busy guards are keyed by ROUTING KEY but the transcript is owned by SESSION_ID, and
``switch_session()`` makes key->id many-to-one (/resume from a second chat, CLI-continuity,
delegation pinning, topic tip-walks), so two keys could interleave flushes on one transcript
(``user;user`` wedge). The lease serializes per RESOLVED session_id: acquired right before the
transcript load, released in the dispatch layer's ``finally``; identity-checked release; a
timed-out waiter fails CLOSED (:class:`TurnLeaseTimeoutError`); only idle entries evict. Limits:
CLI-continuity processes are outside this lock; mid-turn rotation alias is closed by ``rebind``.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import time
from typing import Dict, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Cap on tracked leases. Idle entries evict oldest-first; live leases never do, so a burst of
# distinct sessions may transiently exceed the cap rather than break serialization.
DEFAULT_MAX_LEASES = 512
# Fallback wait (seconds) when the caller passes no positive timeout (bridged via
# HERMES_TURN_LEASE_TIMEOUT — lease contention is not agent inactivity). Fail-closed but short:
# never pin a sequential platform updater for minutes.
DEFAULT_LEASE_WAIT = 5.0


def _holder_desc(holder: Optional["TurnLeaseToken"]) -> tuple:
    return (holder.owner_key, holder.generation) if holder else ("?", "?")


class TurnLeaseTimeoutError(TimeoutError):
    """Lease held for the full wait budget; fail-closed: caller must not enter the turn region."""

    def __init__(self, session_id: str, *, owner_key: str, generation: int, wait_seconds: float):
        self.session_id, self.owner_key = session_id, owner_key
        self.generation, self.wait_seconds = generation, wait_seconds
        super().__init__(f"turn lease wait timed out after {wait_seconds:.0f}s on session "
                         f"{session_id} for routing key {owner_key} (gen {generation})")


class TurnLeaseToken:
    """Held-lease handle from :meth:`SessionTurnLeaseRegistry.acquire`; ``released`` makes
    release idempotent."""

    __slots__ = ("session_id", "owner_key", "generation", "released", "lease")

    def __init__(self, session_id: str, owner_key: str, generation: int, lease: "_SessionLease") -> None:
        self.session_id, self.owner_key, self.generation = session_id, owner_key, generation
        self.released = False
        # The concrete lease, so release resolves by identity even after a rotation re-aliases
        # ``session_id`` (both ids map to this same lease).
        self.lease = lease

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug aid
        return (f"TurnLeaseToken(session_id={self.session_id!r}, owner_key={self.owner_key!r}, "
                f"generation={self.generation}, released={self.released})")


class _SessionLease:
    __slots__ = ("lock", "holder", "acquired_at", "last_used", "pending_acquires")

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self.holder: Optional[TurnLeaseToken] = None
        self.acquired_at, self.last_used, self.pending_acquires = 0.0, time.time(), 0

    @property
    def idle(self) -> bool:
        """True when evictable: nobody holds or awaits it."""
        return self.holder is None and not self.lock.locked() and self.pending_acquires == 0


class SessionTurnLeaseRegistry:
    """Asyncio lease per resolved session_id. Process-local, single-event-loop by design (same
    visibility scope as the routing-key guards it extends); call only from the gateway loop."""

    def __init__(self, max_entries: int = DEFAULT_MAX_LEASES) -> None:
        self._leases: Dict[str, _SessionLease] = {}
        self._max_entries = max(1, int(max_entries))

    def _get_or_create(self, session_id: str) -> _SessionLease:
        if (lease := self._leases.get(session_id)) is None:
            self._evict_idle()
            lease = self._leases[session_id] = _SessionLease()
        lease.last_used = time.time()
        return lease

    def _evict_idle(self) -> None:
        """Drop oldest idle entries to fit a new lease under the cap; never a held/contended one."""
        if (overflow := len(self._leases) - self._max_entries + 1) <= 0:
            return
        idle = sorted((sid for sid, l in self._leases.items() if l.idle),
                      key=lambda sid: self._leases[sid].last_used)
        for sid in idle[:overflow]:
            self._leases.pop(sid, None)

    async def acquire(
        self, session_id: str, *, owner_key: str, generation: int, timeout: Optional[float] = None
    ) -> Optional[TurnLeaseToken]:
        """Acquire the lease for ``session_id``, waiting if held. Raises
        :class:`TurnLeaseTimeoutError` when the wait budget expires; None for a falsy id."""
        if not session_id:
            return None
        wait = float(timeout) if timeout and timeout > 0 else DEFAULT_LEASE_WAIT
        lease = self._get_or_create(session_id)
        token = TurnLeaseToken(session_id, owner_key, int(generation), lease=lease)
        if lease.lock.locked():
            logger.warning(
                "turn lease contention on session %s: routing key %s (gen %s) waiting behind "
                "in-flight turn held by routing key %s (gen %s, held %.0fs) — two routing keys "
                "are mapped to one session_id (#64934); serializing this turn behind the previous "
                "turn's flush",
                session_id, owner_key, generation, *_holder_desc(lease.holder),
                time.time() - lease.acquired_at if lease.acquired_at else -1.0)
        # Lock.release() wakes a waiter while leaving the lock momentarily unlocked. Count every
        # in-progress acquire across that handoff (even apparently-uncontended ones — wait_for()
        # may schedule them before the lock coroutine runs) so eviction cannot orphan the old
        # lock and create a second lock for the same session.
        lease.pending_acquires += 1
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(lease.lock.acquire(), timeout=wait)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            logger.error(
                "turn lease wait timed out after %.0fs on session %s (waiter: routing key %s gen "
                "%s; holder: routing key %s gen %s) — failing closed: refusing to run this turn "
                "UNSERIALIZED against the still-held lease",
                wait, session_id, owner_key, generation, *_holder_desc(lease.holder))
            raise TurnLeaseTimeoutError(
                session_id, owner_key=owner_key, generation=generation, wait_seconds=wait) from None
        finally:
            lease.pending_acquires -= 1
        # Lock held and no await before holder publication, so the lease cannot become
        # evictable after the pending count is cleared.
        lease.holder = token
        lease.acquired_at = lease.last_used = time.time()
        return token

    def rebind(self, token: Optional[TurnLeaseToken], new_session_id: str) -> bool:
        """Alias a HELD lease onto ``new_session_id`` after mid-turn rotation (compression) so the
        flush target stays serialized: the SAME ``_SessionLease`` is registered under the new id
        (old mapping idle-evicts later), only the holder may rebind, the token follows. A live
        lease on the new id: log loudly, keep the old id (fail-open)."""
        if (token is None or token.released or not new_session_id
                or new_session_id == token.session_id):
            return False
        lease = token.lease
        if lease.holder is not token:
            return False
        existing = self._leases.get(new_session_id)
        if existing is not None and existing is not lease and not existing.idle:
            logger.warning(
                "turn lease rebind blocked: session %s rotated to %s mid-turn (holder: routing key "
                "%s gen %s) but the target session's lease is already live (holder: routing key %s "
                "gen %s) — keeping the lease on the old id; transcript writes on %s may "
                "interleave (#64934 rotation-alias edge)",
                token.session_id, new_session_id, token.owner_key, token.generation,
                *_holder_desc(existing.holder), new_session_id)
            return False
        self._leases[new_session_id] = lease
        lease.last_used = time.time()
        token.session_id = new_session_id
        return True

    def release(self, token: Optional[TurnLeaseToken]) -> bool:
        """Release ``token``'s lease. Idempotent; True only when this exact token was the current
        holder (a re-release or a stale token whose slot went to a newer turn is a safe no-op)."""
        if token is None or token.released:
            return False
        token.released = True
        lease = token.lease
        if lease.holder is not token:
            logger.debug("turn lease release skipped on session %s: token (key %s gen %s) is not "
                         "the current holder", token.session_id, token.owner_key, token.generation)
            return False
        lease.holder, lease.acquired_at, lease.last_used = None, 0.0, time.time()
        if lease.lock.locked():
            lease.lock.release()
        return True
"""Behavior tests for the per-session turn lease (#64934).

The lease serializes the [load history → run → flush] region per RESOLVED
session_id, closing the alias-key overlap route: two routing keys mapped to
one session_id via switch_session() run turns on two different agent objects,
invisible to every routing-key guard.

Covers:
- alias-key turn waits until the first turn's flush, and flush order is
  preserved (the second turn loads history AFTER the first turn's release)
- distinct sessions do not contend
- generation-scoped, idempotent release: a stale unwind can never free a
  newer turn's lease; double-release is a no-op
- timeout fail-closed: a timed-out waiter never enters the transcript region,
  and outer dispatch returns a visible rejection/resend notice without invoking
  goal continuation
- registry stays bounded; live and pending leases are never evicted
- timed-out and cancelled acquire attempts do not pin idle registry entries
- GatewayRunner._release_turn_lease wiring (bare-runner safe, token-scoped)
"""

import asyncio
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock

import pytest

from gateway.turn_lease import (
    SessionTurnLeaseRegistry,
    TurnLeaseTimeoutError,
)


def _run(coro):
    return asyncio.run(coro)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Serialization behavior
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_alias_key_turn_waits_and_order_is_preserved():
    """Second routing key on the same session_id waits for the first turn's
    release; events interleave in strict [load1, flush1, load2, flush2] order."""

    async def scenario():
        registry = SessionTurnLeaseRegistry()
        events = []

        async def turn(owner_key, generation, hold):
            token = await registry.acquire(
                "sess-1", owner_key=owner_key, generation=generation, timeout=5
            )
            assert token is not None
            events.append(f"load:{owner_key}")
            await asyncio.sleep(hold)  # simulate run + flush
            events.append(f"flush:{owner_key}")
            registry.release(token)

        t1 = asyncio.create_task(turn("key-a", 1, hold=0.05))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)  # let turn 1 take the lease
        t2 = asyncio.create_task(turn("key-b", 1, hold=0))
        await asyncio.gather(t1, t2)
        return events

    events = _run(scenario())
    assert events == ["load:key-a", "flush:key-a", "load:key-b", "flush:key-b"]


def test_distinct_sessions_do_not_contend():
    async def scenario():
        registry = SessionTurnLeaseRegistry()
        order = []

        async def turn(session_id, owner_key):
            token = await registry.acquire(
                session_id, owner_key=owner_key, generation=1, timeout=5
            )
            order.append(f"start:{session_id}")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
            order.append(f"end:{session_id}")
            registry.release(token)

        await asyncio.gather(turn("sess-a", "key-a"), turn("sess-b", "key-b"))
        return order

    order = _run(scenario())
    # Both started before either finished — no serialization across sessions.
    assert order[:2] == ["start:sess-a", "start:sess-b"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Release semantics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timeout safety
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------




def test_timeout_fails_closed_instead_of_authorizing_an_unserialized_turn():
    """A timed-out waiter must never run against the still-live holder.

    Returning a degraded token used to authorize exactly that unsafe path.
    The two turns could then load the same history base and interleave their
    transcript writes, defeating the serialization invariant this lease owns.
    """

    async def scenario():
        registry = SessionTurnLeaseRegistry()
        holder = await registry.acquire(
            "sess-timeout", owner_key="key-a", generation=1, timeout=1
        )
        assert holder is not None

        with pytest.raises(TurnLeaseTimeoutError):
            await registry.acquire(
                "sess-timeout", owner_key="key-b", generation=1, timeout=0.02
            )

        # The timeout neither steals nor releases the live holder's lease.
        assert registry._leases["sess-timeout"].holder is holder
        assert registry.release(holder) is True

        # Once the holder releases, a later turn can acquire normally.
        successor = await registry.acquire(
            "sess-timeout", owner_key="key-b", generation=2, timeout=1
        )
        assert successor is not None
        assert registry.release(successor) is True

    _run(scenario())

"""Per-session turn lease — serializes the [load history -> run -> flush] region.

Busy guards are keyed by ROUTING KEY but the transcript is owned by SESSION_ID, and
``switch_session()`` makes key->id many-to-one (/resume from a second chat, CLI-continuity,
delegation pinning, topic tip-walks), so two keys could interleave flushes on one transcript
(``user;user`` wedge). The lease serializes per RESOLVED session_id: acquired right before the
transcript load, released in the dispatch layer's ``finally``; identity-checked release; a
timed-out waiter fails CLOSED (:class:`TurnLeaseTimeoutError`); only idle entries evict. Limits:
CLI-continuity processes are outside this lock; mid-turn rotation alias is closed by ``rebind``.
"""

import asyncio
import logging
import time
from typing import Dict, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Cap on tracked leases. Idle entries evict oldest-first; live leases never do, so a burst of
# distinct sessions may transiently exceed the cap rather than break serialization.
DEFAULT_MAX_LEASES = 512
# Fallback wait (seconds) when the caller passes no positive timeout (bridged via
# HERMES_TURN_LEASE_TIMEOUT — lease contention is not agent inactivity). Fail-closed but short:
# never pin a sequential platform updater for minutes.
DEFAULT_LEASE_WAIT = 5.0


def _holder_desc(holder: Optional["TurnLeaseToken"]) -> tuple:
    return (holder.owner_key, holder.generation) if holder else ("?", "?")


class TurnLeaseTimeoutError(TimeoutError):
    """Lease held for the full wait budget; fail-closed: caller must not enter the turn region."""

    def __init__(self, session_id: str, *, owner_key: str, generation: int, wait_seconds: float):
        self.session_id, self.owner_key = session_id, owner_key
        self.generation, self.wait_seconds = generation, wait_seconds
        super().__init__(f"turn lease wait timed out after {wait_seconds:.0f}s on session "
                         f"{session_id} for routing key {owner_key} (gen {generation})")


class TurnLeaseToken:
    """Held-lease handle from :meth:`SessionTurnLeaseRegistry.acquire`; ``released`` makes
    release idempotent."""

    __slots__ = ("session_id", "owner_key", "generation", "released", "lease")

    def __init__(self, session_id: str, owner_key: str, generation: int, lease: "_SessionLease") -> None:
        self.session_id, self.owner_key, self.generation = session_id, owner_key, generation
        self.released = False
        # The concrete lease, so release resolves by identity even after a rotation re-aliases
        # ``session_id`` (both ids map to this same lease).
        self.lease = lease

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debug aid
        return (f"TurnLeaseToken(session_id={self.session_id!r}, owner_key={self.owner_key!r}, "
                f"generation={self.generation}, released={self.released})")


class _SessionLease:
    __slots__ = ("lock", "holder", "acquired_at", "last_used", "pending_acquires")

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self.holder: Optional[TurnLeaseToken] = None
        self.acquired_at, self.last_used, self.pending_acquires = 0.0, time.time(), 0

    @property
    def idle(self) -> bool:
        """True when evictable: nobody holds or awaits it."""
        return self.holder is None and not self.lock.locked() and self.pending_acquires == 0


class SessionTurnLeaseRegistry:
    """Asyncio lease per resolved session_id. Process-local, single-event-loop by design (same
    visibility scope as the routing-key guards it extends); call only from the gateway loop."""

    def __init__(self, max_entries: int = DEFAULT_MAX_LEASES) -> None:
        self._leases: Dict[str, _SessionLease] = {}
        self._max_entries = max(1, int(max_entries))

    def _get_or_create(self, session_id: str) -> _SessionLease:
        if (lease := self._leases.get(session_id)) is None:
            self._evict_idle()
            lease = self._leases[session_id] = _SessionLease()
        lease.last_used = time.time()
        return lease

    def _evict_idle(self) -> None:
        """Drop oldest idle entries to fit a new lease under the cap; never a held/contended one."""
        if (overflow := len(self._leases) - self._max_entries + 1) <= 0:
            return
        idle = sorted((sid for sid, l in self._leases.items() if l.idle),
                      key=lambda sid: self._leases[sid].last_used)
        for sid in idle[:overflow]:
            self._leases.pop(sid, None)

    async def acquire(
        self, session_id: str, *, owner_key: str, generation: int, timeout: Optional[float] = None
    ) -> Optional[TurnLeaseToken]:
        """Acquire the lease for ``session_id``, waiting if held. Raises
        :class:`TurnLeaseTimeoutError` when the wait budget expires; None for a falsy id."""
        if not session_id:
            return None
        wait = float(timeout) if timeout and timeout > 0 else DEFAULT_LEASE_WAIT
        lease = self._get_or_create(session_id)
        token = TurnLeaseToken(session_id, owner_key, int(generation), lease=lease)
        if lease.lock.locked():
            logger.warning(
                "turn lease contention on session %s: routing key %s (gen %s) waiting behind "
                "in-flight turn held by routing key %s (gen %s, held %.0fs) — two routing keys "
                "are mapped to one session_id (#64934); serializing this turn behind the previous "
                "turn's flush",
                session_id, owner_key, generation, *_holder_desc(lease.holder),
                time.time() - lease.acquired_at if lease.acquired_at else -1.0)
        # Lock.release() wakes a waiter while leaving the lock momentarily unlocked. Count every
        # in-progress acquire across that handoff (even apparently-uncontended ones — wait_for()
        # may schedule them before the lock coroutine runs) so eviction cannot orphan the old
        # lock and create a second lock for the same session.
        lease.pending_acquires += 1
        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(lease.lock.acquire(), timeout=wait)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            logger.error(
                "turn lease wait timed out after %.0fs on session %s (waiter: routing key %s gen "
                "%s; holder: routing key %s gen %s) — failing closed: refusing to run this turn "
                "UNSERIALIZED against the still-held lease",
                wait, session_id, owner_key, generation, *_holder_desc(lease.holder))
            raise TurnLeaseTimeoutError(
                session_id, owner_key=owner_key, generation=generation, wait_seconds=wait) from None
        finally:
            lease.pending_acquires -= 1
        # Lock held and no await before holder publication, so the lease cannot become
        # evictable after the pending count is cleared.
        lease.holder = token
        lease.acquired_at = lease.last_used = time.time()
        return token

    def rebind(self, token: Optional[TurnLeaseToken], new_session_id: str) -> bool:
        """Alias a HELD lease onto ``new_session_id`` after mid-turn rotation (compression) so the
        flush target stays serialized: the SAME ``_SessionLease`` is registered under the new id
        (old mapping idle-evicts later), only the holder may rebind, the token follows. A live
        lease on the new id: log loudly, keep the old id (fail-open)."""
        if (token is None or token.released or not new_session_id
                or new_session_id == token.session_id):
            return False
        lease = token.lease
        if lease.holder is not token:
            return False
        existing = self._leases.get(new_session_id)
        if existing is not None and existing is not lease and not existing.idle:
            logger.warning(
                "turn lease rebind blocked: session %s rotated to %s mid-turn (holder: routing key "
                "%s gen %s) but the target session's lease is already live (holder: routing key %s "
                "gen %s) — keeping the lease on the old id; transcript writes on %s may "
                "interleave (#64934 rotation-alias edge)",
                token.session_id, new_session_id, token.owner_key, token.generation,
                *_holder_desc(existing.holder), new_session_id)
            return False
        self._leases[new_session_id] = lease
        lease.last_used = time.time()
        token.session_id = new_session_id
        return True

    def release(self, token: Optional[TurnLeaseToken]) -> bool:
        """Release ``token``'s lease. Idempotent; True only when this exact token was the current
        holder (a re-release or a stale token whose slot went to a newer turn is a safe no-op)."""
        if token is None or token.released:

L85: In this guide, you will deploy a Worker that can make requests to one or more Containers in response to end-user requests. In this example, each container runs a small webserver written in Go.
L86: 
L87: This example Worker should give you a sense for simple Container use, and provide a starting point for more complex use cases.
L88: This guide uses the `Container` class and its built-in lifecycle helpers. You can also manage containers directly through `ctx.container`. To compare both options, refer to cite21†Containers APIs .
L89: ## Prerequisites
L90: ### Ensure Docker is running locally
L91: 
L92: In this guide, we will build and push a container image alongside your Worker code. By default, this process uses cite47†Docker ↗︎†www.docker.com to do so.
L93: 
L94: You must have Docker running locally when you run `wrangler deploy`. For most people, the best way to install Docker is to follow the cite48†docs for installing Docker Desktop ↗︎†docs.docker.com . Other tools like cite49†Colima ↗︎†github.com may also work.
L95: You can check that Docker is running properly by running the `docker info` command in your terminal. If Docker is running, the command will succeed. If Docker is not running, the `docker info` command will hang or return an error including the message "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon".
L96: ## Deploy your first Container
L97: 
L98: Run the following command to create and deploy a new Worker with a container, from the starter template:
L99: 
L100: [Button: npm][Button: yarn][Button: pnpm]
L101: 
L102:     `npm create cloudflare@latest -- --template=cloudflare/templates/containers-template`
L103: 
L104:     `yarn create cloudflare --template=cloudflare/templates/containers-template`
L105: 
L106:     `pnpm create cloudflare@latest --template=cloudflare/templates/containers-template`
L107: When you want to deploy a code change to either the Worker or Container code, you can run the following command using cite50†Wrangler CLI :
L108: 
L109: [Button: npm][Button: yarn][Button: pnpm]
L110: 
L111:     `npx wrangler deploy`
L112: 
L113:     `yarn wrangler deploy`
L114: 
L115:     `pnpm wrangler deploy`
L116: On deploy, Wrangler uploads your Worker, builds and pushes the container image with Docker, and updates container instances on Cloudflare's network. The first build and push usually take the longest. Later deploys cite51†reuse cached image layers ↗︎†docs.docker.com .
L117: 
L118: Note
L119: After you deploy your Worker for the first time, wait several minutes before you expect container requests to succeed. The Worker URL may respond while Cloudflare is still provisioning containers. During that time, calls into the container can error.
L120: ### Check deployment status
L121: 
L122: After deploying, list containers in your account and their status:
L123: 
L124: [Button: npm][Button: yarn][Button: pnpm]
L125: 
L126:     `npx wrangler containers list`
L127: 
L128:     `yarn wrangler containers list`
L129: 
L130:     `pnpm wrangler containers list`
L131: 
L132: List images in the Cloudflare Registry:
L133: 
L134: [Button: npm][Button: yarn][Button: pnpm]
L135: 
L136:     `npx wrangler containers images list`
L137: 
L138:     `yarn wrangler containers images list`
L139: 
L140:     `pnpm wrangler containers images list`
L141: ### Make requests to Containers
L142: 
L143: Open the URL for your Worker. It should look like `https://hello-containers.<YOUR_WORKERS_SUBDOMAIN>.workers.dev`.
L144: 
L145:   * Requests to `/container/1` or `/container/2` route to specific containers. Each path after `/container/` maps to a unique container.
L146:   * Requests to `/lb` load-balance across three containers chosen at random.
L147: Read the response body to confirm which instance handled the request. If the Worker responds but container routes still error, wait for provisioning, then check cite52†Containers ↗︎†dash.cloudflare.com logs in the dashboard.
L148: ## Understanding the Code
L149: 
L150: Now that you've deployed your first container, let's explain what is happening in your Worker's code, in your configuration file, in your container's code, and how requests are routed.
L151: ### Configuration
L152: Your cite14†Wrangler configuration file defines the configuration for both your Worker and your container:
L153: 
L154:     `{
L155:     	"containers": [
L156:     		{
L157:     			"max_instances": 10,
L158:     			"class_name": "MyContainer",
L159:     			"image": "./Dockerfile",
L160:     		},
L161:     	],
L162:     	"durable_objects": {
L163:     		"bindings": [
L164:     			{
L165:     				"name": "MY_CONTAINER",
L166:     				"class_name": "MyContainer",
L167:     			},
L168:     		],
L169:     	},
L170:     	"exports": {
L171:     		"MyContainer": {
L172:     			"type": "durable-object",
L173:     			"storage": "sqlite",
L174:     		},
L175:     	},
L176:     }`
L177: 
L178:     `[[containers]]
L179:     max_instances = 10
L180:     class_name = "MyContainer"
L181:     image = "./Dockerfile"
L182: 
L183:     [[durable_objects.bindings]]
L184:     name = "MY_CONTAINER"
L185:     class_name = "MyContainer"
L186: 
L187:     [exports.MyContainer]
L188:     type = "durable-object"
L189:     storage = "sqlite"`
L190: Important points about this config:
L191:   * `image` points to a Dockerfile, to a directory containing a Dockerfile, or to a fully qualified image reference such as `registry.cloudflare.com/<YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID>/<IMAGE>:<TAG>`.
L192:   * `class_name` must be a cite53†Durable Object class name .
L193:   * `max_instances` declares the maximum number of simultaneously running container instances that will run.
L194:   * The `exports` entry declares the Durable Object class with SQLite storage. Existing applications that use the legacy `migrations` array can continue to use it, but `exports` and `migrations` cannot be combined.
L195: ### The Container Image
L196: 
L197: Your container image must be able to run on the `linux/amd64` architecture, but aside from that, has few limitations.
L198: In the example you just deployed, it is a simple Golang server that responds to requests on port 8080 using the `MESSAGE` environment variable that will be set in the Worker and an cite17†auto-generated environment variable `CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOYMENT_ID.`
L199: 
L200:     `func handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
L201:     	message := os.Getenv("MESSAGE")
L202:     	instanceId := os.Getenv("CLOUDFLARE_DEPLOYMENT_ID")
L203:     	fmt.Fprintf(w, "Hi, I'm a container and this is my message: %s, and my instance ID is: %s", message, instanceId)
L204:     }`
L205: Note
L206: 
L207: After deploying the example code, to deploy a different image, you can replace the provided image with one of your own.
L208: ### Worker code
L209: #### Container Configuration
L210: First note `MyContainer` which extends the cite54†`Container` ↗︎†github.com class:
L211: 
L212:     `export class MyContainer extends Container {
L213:       defaultPort = 8080;
L214:       sleepAfter = '10s';
L215:       envVars = {
L216:         MESSAGE: 'I was passed in via the container class!',
L217:       };
L218: 
L219:       override onStart() {
L220:         console.log('Container successfully started');
L221:       }
L222: 
L223:       override onStop() {
L224:         console.log('Container successfully shut down');
L225:       }
L226:       override onError(error: unknown) {
L227:         console.log('Container error:', error);
L228:       }
L229:     }`
L230: This defines basic configuration for the container:
L231:   * `defaultPort` sets the port that the `fetch` and `containerFetch` methods will use to communicate with the container. It also blocks requests until the container is listening on this port.
L232:   * `sleepAfter` sets the timeout for the container to sleep after it has been idle for a certain amount of time.
L233:   * `envVars` sets environment variables that will be passed to the container when it starts.
L234:   * `onStart`, `onStop`, and `onError` are hooks that run when the container starts, stops, or errors, respectively.
L235: The `Container` class itself extends cite55†`DurableObject` , so your subclass has access to the full Durable Object API. The Durable Object handles routing, lifecycle, and persistent state, while the container process runs your image inside a Linux VM. This means you can use cite56†`this.ctx.storage` to persist data that survives container restarts and resides close to the container itself.
L236: 
L237: For all properties and methods, refer to the cite23†Container class API and the cite22†Durable Object Container API .
L238: #### Routing to Containers
L239: 
L240: When a request enters Cloudflare, your Worker's cite57†`fetch` handler is invoked. This is the code that handles the incoming request. The fetch handler in the example code, launches containers in two ways, on different routes:
L241:   * Making requests to `/container/` passes requests to a new container for each path. This is done by spinning up a new Container instance. You may note that the first request to a new path takes longer than subsequent requests, this is because a new container is booting.
L242: 
L243:     `if (pathname.startsWith("/container")) {
L244:     	const container = env.MY_CONTAINER.getByName(pathname);
L245:     	return await container.fetch(request);
L246:     }`
L247:   * Making requests to `/lb` will load balance requests across several containers. This uses a simple `getRandom` helper method, which picks an ID at random from a set number (in this case 3), then routes to that Container instance. You can replace this with any routing or load balancing logic you choose to implement:
L248: 
L249:     `if (pathname.startsWith("/lb")) {
L250:     	const container = await getRandom(env.MY_CONTAINER, 3);
L251:     	return await container.fetch(request);
L252:     }`
L253: This allows for multiple ways of using Containers:
L254:   * If you simply want to send requests to many stateless and interchangeable containers, you should load balance.
L255:   * If you have stateful services or need individually addressable containers, you should request specific Container instances.
L256:   * If you are running short-lived jobs, want fine-grained control over the container lifecycle, want to parameterize container entrypoint or env vars, or want to chain together multiple container calls, you should request specific Container instances.
L257: 
L258: Note
L259: Today, routing requests to one of many interchangeable Container instances uses the `getRandom` helper.
L260: 
L261: It randomly selects one of a fixed number of instances for each request.
L262: ## View Containers in your Dashboard
L263: 
L264: The cite52†Containers Dashboard ↗︎†dash.cloudflare.com shows you helpful information about your Containers, including:
L265: 
L266:   * Status and Health
L267:   * Metrics
L268:   * Logs
L269: 
L270: After launching your Worker, go to the Containers Dashboard by selecting Workers & Pages > Containers in the dashboard sidebar.
L271: ## Next Steps
L272: 
L273: To do more:
L274: 
L275:   * Modify the image by changing the Dockerfile and running `wrangler deploy`
L276:   * Refer to cite6†Deploy Containers for Workers Builds and rollout behavior
L277:   * Browse cite58†examples for more patterns
L278:   * Check the cite34†Frequently Asked Questions for platform behavior and limitations

L602: A `monitor()` promise does not carry over when the Durable Object restarts, for example after a deploy. If `running` is `true` when the Durable Object starts, call `monitor()` again to observe the container.
L603: #### Parameters
L604: 
L605:   * None.
L606: #### Return values
L607:   * `Promise<void>`: Settles when the container stops, including a container that stopped before the call. The outcome depends on how the container stopped:
L608:     * It resolves when the main process exits with code `0`, or when `destroy()` stops the container without an error value.
L609:     * It rejects with an `Error` that has an `exitCode` property when the main process exits with another code.
L610:     * It rejects with the value passed to `destroy()`, when there is one.
L611:     * It rejects with an error that describes the failure when the container stops for another reason.
L612: #### Exceptions
L613: 
L614:   * `monitor()` throws an `Error` when this Durable Object instance has no container. An instance has a container after it calls `start()`, or when a container was already running as the instance started.
L615: ### `interceptOutboundHttp`
L616: `interceptOutboundHttp()` routes outbound HTTP requests matching a hostname, hostname glob, IP address, IP:port, or CIDR range through a `Fetcher`. Call it before or after starting the container. An intercept lasts until the container stops, so register intercepts again for each new container. Registering a target again replaces its handler, and open connections use the new handler without being dropped.
L617: 
L618:     `const worker = this.ctx.exports.MyWorker({ props: { message: "hello" } });
L619:     // Match a specific hostname
L620:     await this.ctx.container.interceptOutboundHttp("api.example.com", worker);
L621: 
L622:     // Match a hostname glob pattern
L623:     await this.ctx.container.interceptOutboundHttp("*.example.com", worker);
L624: 
L625:     // Match an IP:port
L626:     await this.ctx.container.interceptOutboundHttp("15.0.0.1:80", worker);
L627: 
L628:     // Match an IPv4 CIDR range. Register an IPv6 range separately.
L629:     await this.ctx.container.interceptOutboundHttp("203.0.113.0/24", worker);`
L630: In a container started with `enableInternet: false`, no public resolver answers DNS lookups. Lookups resolve as follows:
L631:   * `A` and `AAAA` lookups for an intercepted hostname return a placeholder address that routes the request to the intercept.
L632:   * `interceptAllOutboundHttp()` and a `*` hostname target make every hostname resolve, including hostnames that do not exist.
L633:   * IP address and CIDR targets add no DNS answers, except for `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0`, which make every hostname resolve.
L634:   * Every other lookup times out, including a lookup made before you register an intercept.

L81: 
L82: Last updated Sep 29, 2026|Copy as Markdown|cite46†View as Markdown |cite37†Agent setup L83: 
L84: [Select]
L85: 
L86: Define Containers in the Wrangler configuration file for your Worker. Each Container is associated with a Durable Object class, which provides access to the Container at runtime.
L87: ## Minimal configuration
L88: A new Container application requires a Container definition, a Durable Object binding, and a Durable Object class export:
L89: 
L90:     `{
L91:     	"$schema": "./node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",
L92:     	"name": "my-container-worker",
L93:     	"main": "src/index.ts",
L94:     	// Set this to today's date
L95:     	"compatibility_date": "2026-10-03",
L96:     	"containers": [
L97:     		{
L98:     			"class_name": "MyContainer",
L99:     			"image": "./Dockerfile",
L100:     			"max_instances": 10,
L101:     		},
L102:     	],
L103:     	"durable_objects": {
L104:     		"bindings": [
L105:     			{
L106:     				"name": "MY_CONTAINER",
L107:     				"class_name": "MyContainer",
L108:     			},
L109:     		],
L110:     	},
L111:     	"exports": {
L112:     		"MyContainer": {
L113:     			"type": "durable-object",
L114:     			"storage": "sqlite",
L115:     		},
L116:     	},
L117:     }`
L118: 
L119:     `"$schema" = "./node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json"
L120:     name = "my-container-worker"
L121:     main = "src/index.ts"
L122:     # Set this to today's date
L123:     compatibility_date = "2026-10-03"
L124: 
L125:     [[containers]]
L126:     class_name = "MyContainer"
L127:     image = "./Dockerfile"
L128:     max_instances = 10
L129: 
L130:     [[durable_objects.bindings]]
L131:     name = "MY_CONTAINER"
L132:     class_name = "MyContainer"
L133: 
L134:     [exports.MyContainer]
L135:     type = "durable-object"
L136:     storage = "sqlite"`
L137: The configuration uses three sections:
L138: 
L139:   1. `containers` defines the container image and associates it with a Durable Object class through `class_name`.
L140:   2. `durable_objects.bindings` makes the Durable Object namespace available to Worker code. In this example, access it through `env.MY_CONTAINER`.
L141:   3. `exports` declares the Durable Object class and provisions it with SQLite storage.
L142: The `class_name` in `containers` and `durable_objects.bindings`, and the key in `exports`, must match the exported Durable Object class in your Worker.
L143: 
L144: Existing applications
L145: 
L146: Existing applications that use the legacy `migrations` array can continue to use it. Do not configure `exports` and `migrations` together. To switch an existing application to `exports`, refer to cite47†Migrate from the legacy `migrations` flow .
L147: ## Container settings
L148: 
L149: The `containers` entry can also configure the instance type, maximum number of running instances, image build, placement constraints, rollouts, and SSH access.
L150: 
L151: For all available fields and values, refer to the cite32†Containers Wrangler configuration reference .
L152: ## Next steps
L153: 
L154:   * cite6†Deploy Containers — Build the image and deploy the Worker.
L155:   * cite18†Scaling and Routing — Route requests and scale Container instances.
L156:   * cite19†Rollouts — Control how configuration changes reach running instances.
L157:   * cite9†Image management — Use local and remote container images.

L80: # Use snapshots
L81: 
L82: Last updated Sep 30, 2026|Copy as Markdown|cite46†View as Markdown |cite37†Agent setup L83: 
L84: [Select]
L85: 
L86: Snapshots let you save point-in-time filesystem state from a running cite1†Container . The examples on this page use the cite22†Durable Object Container API .
L87: 
L88: Scheduling policy requirement
L89: 
L90: Snapshots are only supported by Container applications that use the cite47†`durable_object` scheduling policy . Applications that use the `default` scheduling policy cannot create or restore snapshots.
L91: ## Create a container snapshot
L92: 
L93: Use `snapshotContainer()` to capture the full container filesystem. Snapshots are immutable. If you restore a snapshot and then change files, create a new snapshot to persist those changes.
L94: 
L95: Snapshot image compatibility
L96: Snapshots capture the Container's complete filesystem state, but not its memory or running processes. A snapshot is tied to the Container image version it was created from and is not portable to a different image. After updating the image, create a new snapshot from a Container running that image.
L97: 
L98: The returned snapshot handle is a plain data object. You can store it and restore it later, including from another Durable Object:
L99: src/index.js js
L100: 
L101:     `import { DurableObject } from "cloudflare:workers";

L86: A scheduling policy determines where you configure a Container image and cite47†instance size . It also determines how image updates and cite19†rollouts apply. Choose the policy when you create the Container application.
L87: Policy  | Configure image and instance size  | Image updates  | Best for
L88: --- | --- | --- | ---
L89: `default`  | In Wrangler configuration  | Cloudflare applies application-wide configuration changes with cite19†rollouts | Services whose instances use the same image and instance size
L90: `durable_object` (beta)  | In Durable Object code when calling `ctx.container.start()`  | Application code selects an image each time it starts an instance  | Sandboxes, agent environments, and other workloads that need per-instance configuration
L91: Note
L92: 
L93: The `durable_object` scheduling policy is in public beta.
L94: 
L95: One Wrangler configuration can contain applications with both policies. This lets a Worker use centrally managed service Containers alongside Durable Object-managed sandboxes.
L96: The scheduling policy is immutable. To use a different policy, create a new Container application. Deleting an application also deletes its Container instances, so switching policies means replacing every running instance. To move an existing application, refer to cite13†Migrate to the Durable Object scheduling policy .
L97: ## Use the default scheduling policy
L98: With the `default` policy, Wrangler configuration defines one application-wide `image`, one cite47†`instance_type` , and settings such as `max_instances`. Omitting `scheduling_policy` selects `default`.
L99: 
L100:     `{
L101:     	"containers": [
L102:     		{
L103:     			"class_name": "ApiContainer",
L104:     			"scheduling_policy": "default",
L105:     			"image": "./api/Dockerfile",
L106:     			"instance_type": "standard-1",
L107:     			"max_instances": 5,
L108:     		},
L109:     	],
L110:     }`
L111: 
L112:     `[[containers]]
L113:     class_name = "ApiContainer"
L114:     scheduling_policy = "default"
L115:     image = "./api/Dockerfile"
L116:     instance_type = "standard-1"
L117:     max_instances = 5`
L118: When you change the image or instance type and deploy, Cloudflare rolls out that change across the application. Refer to cite19†Rollouts .
L119: ## Use the Durable Object scheduling policy
L120: 
L121: The `durable_object` policy moves per-instance decisions into your Durable Object. Wrangler associates the Container application with the Durable Object class, and your code supplies a startup image or snapshot and an optional instance size to `ctx.container.start()`.
L122: Configure the policy. To use custom images, add the images that the Durable Object can start:
L123: 
L124:     `{
L125:     	"name": "agent-computer",
L126:     	"main": "src/index.ts",
L127:     	"compatibility_date": "2026-09-29",
L128:     	"containers": [
L129:     		{
L130:     			"class_name": "AgentComputer",
L131:     			"scheduling_policy": "durable_object",
L132:     			"images": {
L133:     				"base": {
L134:     					"dockerfile": "./container/Dockerfile",
L135:     				},
L136:     			},
L137:     		},
L138:     	],
L139:     	"durable_objects": {
L140:     		"bindings": [
L141:     			{
L142:     				"name": "AGENT_COMPUTER",
L143:     				"class_name": "AgentComputer",
L144:     			},
L145:     		],
L146:     	},
L147:     	"exports": {
L148:     		"AgentComputer": {
L149:     			"type": "durable-object",
L150:     			"storage": "sqlite",
L151:     		},
L152:     	},
L153:     }`
L154: 
L155:     `name = "agent-computer"
L156:     main = "src/index.ts"
L157:     compatibility_date = "2026-09-29"
L158: 
L159:     [[containers]]
L160:     class_name = "AgentComputer"
L161:     scheduling_policy = "durable_object"
L162: 
L163:     [containers.images.base]
L164:     dockerfile = "./container/Dockerfile"
L165:     [[durable_objects.bindings]]
L166:     name = "AGENT_COMPUTER"
L167:     class_name = "AgentComputer"
L168: 
L169:     [exports.AgentComputer]
L170:     type = "durable-object"
L171:     storage = "sqlite"`
L172: Wrangler builds or resolves each named image, prepares it for the Containers runtime, and exposes its digest-pinned reference on `ctx.container.images`. Select an image and instance size when the Durable Object starts its Container:
L173: src/index.js js
L174: 
L175:     `import { DurableObject } from "cloudflare:workers";
L176: 
L177:     export class AgentComputer extends DurableObject {
L178:     	startContainer() {
L179:     		if (this.ctx.container.running) {
L180:     			return;
L181:     		}
L182: 
L183:     		this.ctx.container.start({
L184:     			image: this.ctx.container.images.base,
L185:     			instance: "standard-2",
L186:     			enableInternet: false,
L187:     		});
L188:     	}
L189:     }`
L190: src/index.ts ts
L191: 
L192:     `import { DurableObject } from "cloudflare:workers";
L193: 
L194:     export class AgentComputer extends DurableObject {
L195:     	startContainer() {
L196:     		if (this.ctx.container.running) {
L197:     			return;
L198:     		}
L199: 
L200:     		this.ctx.container.start({
L201:     			image: this.ctx.container.images.base,
L202:     			instance: "standard-2",
L203:     			enableInternet: false,
L204:     		});
L205:     	}
L206:     }`
L207: `ctx.container.start()` initiates startup and returns before the Container is ready to accept requests. Add an application-specific readiness check before sending traffic or calling cite48†`exec()` .
L208: 
L209: The `durable_object` policy does not support `max_instances`. Running instances count toward your cite49†account limits .
L210: ### Use the Cloudflare-managed image
L211: 
L212: If you do not need a custom image, start the cite50†`cloudflare/debian-trixie` Cloudflare-managed image directly without adding a named image to Wrangler. It includes Node.js 24.20.0 on Debian Trixie slim:
L213: 
L214: src/index.js js
L215: 
L216:     `this.ctx.container.start({
L217:     	image: "cloudflare/debian-trixie",
L218:     	instance: "standard-2",
L219:     	enableInternet: false,
L220:     });`

L224:     	image: "cloudflare/debian-trixie",
L225:     	instance: "standard-2",
L226:     	enableInternet: false,
L227:     });`

# Cloudflare control-plane preparation

**Local candidate only, 2026-10-04. No deployment, billing change, runtime start, Slack send, or account credential is included.** The user's current scope is three people (Tanishq, Sahan, Nishank), independent simultaneous browser tasks, and free-only investigation. This folder does not select the eventual runtime topology or amend the gateway PRD.

## Implemented and deliberately blocked

- A narrow Worker health endpoint reports `preparation_only`, never runtime readiness.
- An operator-only admin surface reserves, lists, and cancels **unstarted** runtime assignments. One fixed coordinator Durable Object persists the registry before acknowledging a mutation. Concurrent allocation is serialized; configured capacity is 1–3, with a hard ceiling of 3.
- Owners come from a fixed alias set and a trusted workspace/member mapping. Public input cannot supply a workspace, Slack identity, DO name, storage key, image, command, URL, or environment. Opaque reservation IDs and increasing generations are server-generated.
- Admin use is disabled by default; allowlist is empty, the workspace is a placeholder, and no admin secret is supplied. No public Worker routes or preview URL are enabled in the template.
- Runtime start/stop/snapshot/restore, arbitrary exec/proxying, Slack intake, model access, browser control, scheduling/fairness, and Hermes remote dispatch are **not implemented**. Those paths return `501` after authentication. An assignment is not a running VM, a task, or a browser session.

This reservation lifecycle is independently useful preparation. It does not prove that three owners need three permanent VMs: assignments are created on demand, and no container exists in this template. The three-slot bound currently applies to reservation records; a later executor must consume the same authority to enforce the actual runtime bound.

## Files and local checks

The code has no third-party dependencies. Node 24 can execute the TypeScript source used by the tests. A locally installed TypeScript compiler checks the handwritten minimal runtime interfaces; these interfaces are **not** generated Cloudflare types and do not establish platform API compatibility.

From this directory:

```sh
node --test test/control-plane.test.mjs
tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json
```

No install, cloud CLI, live SDK, real credential file, or network request is needed. Test IDs and the test credential are synthetic. Tests instantiate the same Worker/DO classes against in-memory storage; the fake concurrency gate tests application sequencing, not Cloudflare's implementation. A reconstructed class reads saved fixture state, not a cloud restart.

Wrangler is not bundled or invoked. Before using a future installed version, inspect `wrangler --help` and the help for the intended command. Validate the schema, generate current Workers types, and perform a local runtime check before considering any deployment. The `exports` configuration follows current docs and must not be combined with legacy `migrations`.

## Admission and operator API

`GET /health` is inert liveness. Every other route requires HTTPS, `PREP_ADMIN_ENABLED=true`, a valid configured workspace/owner map, and a privately provisioned `CONTROL_ADMIN_SECRET` of at least 32 characters in `Authorization: Bearer …`. Browser-origin requests are denied. No cookies, CORS, credential defaults, or secrets in URLs are supported. Do not give this operator secret to models, browsers, workers, or Slack users.

| Route | JSON body | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /admin/reservations` | none | List preparation assignments |
| `POST /admin/reservations` | `{ "owner": "sahan" }` | Idempotently reserve one unstarted assignment for an admitted owner |
| `DELETE /admin/reservations` | `owner`, `reservationId`, `generation` from its current record | Cancel only the matching **unstarted** reservation |

The caller is a trusted operator, not an authenticated Slack person. This API does not authorize Sahan to control Tanishq's tasks. Future Slack admission must validate transport identity and independently bind requester, resource owner, and audience. Identity-map changes require reconciliation of existing records. Do not reinterpret cancellation as permission to destroy a running runtime.

## Container lifecycle and persistence contract to implement next

The template has **no `containers` block**. Current Cloudflare pricing lists no Containers usage on the Free plan, so a free Worker does not imply free browser hosting. Keep paid execution blocked under the present constraint. [Pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/).

If later authorized, the snapshot-capable candidate is a new application with `scheduling_policy: "durable_object"`. That policy is immutable, uses direct `ctx.container` operations, and does **not** support `max_instances`: the authoritative coordinator must retain a slot for every starting/running/uncertain attempt. Do not add an ineffective `max_instances: 3` to that policy. `basic` is absent from its supported start instance names; measure whether a supported type fits three browser workloads. This is a policy-specific restriction, not a statement that all Cloudflare containers lack `basic`. [Scheduling policies](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/configuration/scheduling-policy/).

Required state transitions:

1. Authenticated admission → durable task and owner/context mapping → bounded assignment with generation/fencing authority.
2. Validate the owner's credential grant and expected checkpoint identity. Restore into a clean runtime using the trusted owner, generation, and manifest digest from the controller. Never accept those values or an R2 key from agent output. Coordinate with [the persistence preparation](../persistence/).
3. Start the pinned runtime and separately verify readiness. A process marked `running` is not an authenticated, initialized Hermes/browser service. Dispatch only after the owner binding and restored state are verified.
4. Renew a bounded task lease. An outbound Slack WebSocket is not a proof that its managing DO remains alive; explicitly implement the transport host's keepalive and reconnect policy. Direct API inactivity timeout must be reapplied after DO reconstruction, and monitoring must be reattached. Do not use unbounded keepalive under a free-only assumption. [Direct Container API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/api/durable-object-container/).
5. Before release, quiesce Hermes/browser writers, close or consistently back up SQLite, publish and verify the checkpoint, then stop. Retain uncertain assignments for reconciliation. A stale attempt cannot publish state or release a newer generation's slot. Do not reuse a dirty runtime across owners.

Native snapshots preserve filesystem state, not memory, open pages, or unfinished actions; mounted filesystems are outside the snapshot. Snapshots depend on image version, and handles have a 30-day TTL refreshed by restore. Store snapshot ownership, generation, image identity, and expiry metadata in trusted durable records. This is an alternative to the proposed versioned R2 bundle transport, not an implemented second backup path. [Snapshots](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/guides/snapshots/).

No guarantee of preserving permissions between Unix users inside one direct-policy container is assumed. Do not use a UID switch as the owner isolation boundary. [Direct API process-user limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/api/durable-object-container/#exec).

## Acceptance still required

| Stage | Evidence required |
| --- | --- |
| Local application checks | Default denial, strict body schema, no caller-selected runtime, three simultaneous distinct reservations, duplicate idempotency, cap, stale cancellation denial, storage failure and corrupt-state refusal |
| Platform preflight | Current Wrangler schema/types, account capability and free-only feasibility, actual DO storage/concurrency behavior, no unintended public route, operator secret provisioning procedure |
| Three-owner browser execution | Three simultaneous tasks, distinct browser/profile/private files, no cross-owner cookies or recall, scoped credential release, no broad Slack/cloud tokens inside agent execution |
| Persistence/recovery | Fresh-worker restore, image compatibility, deleted/expired checkpoint refusal, quiescent snapshot, interrupted task reconciliation, stale-generation fencing, retention/backups |
| Slack gateway | Authenticated workspace/sender/surface gate, deny unknown owner, durable ACK boundary, restart-safe deduplication, fixed reply audience, owner-bound approval/cancel, reconnect and delivery retry without duplicate execution |

None of the local reservation tests pass these platform, browser, persistence, or Slack acceptance rows. Shared gateway concurrency itself is already supported by pinned Hermes; the unresolved work is the execution boundary and its lifecycle, not creating a separate Slack connection for each person.

item.stdout:
# Hermes persistence prototype and restart contract

Status: **local dummy-data prototype; cloud transport and runtime lifecycle are not implemented**. Reviewed 2026-10-04. No real credentials or browser profiles were read, exported, restored, or uploaded. The pinned Hermes checkout is unchanged; this utility does not replace its agent loop, tools, browser driver, or gateway.

## What is executable now

Run the independent dummy-data tests from the repository root:

```sh
.local/hermes-lab/venv/bin/python -B deployment/cloudflare/persistence/test_snapshot_fixture.py
```

`snapshot_fixture.py` provides offline `export` and `restore` commands. Inspect their help before using them. Exports require an explicit include list, `--quiescent`, `--allow-dummy-private-data`, and a source marker named `.clanker-dummy-fixture` whose exact content is `CLANKER DUMMY DATA ONLY\n`. **Do not put that marker in a real Hermes home.** Tests create and remove all dummy homes under a temporary directory.

The include list is relative to exactly one private home. A future live adapter must inventory all durable paths used by the selected upstream configuration; this fixture utility does not discover a complete Hermes backup set. The tests select `state.db`, `config.yaml`, fake `auth.json`, a file directory, and a fake browser-profile directory. No source home is inferred from environment variables.

Exports use SQLite's [online backup API](https://www.sqlite.org/backup.html), through Python's [`Connection.backup`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/sqlite3.html#sqlite3.Connection.backup), for files with a SQLite header. This includes committed WAL contents and produces a standalone database; copying only a live `.db` file is insufficient. Database-suffixed files with an invalid header are refused. Quiescence remains required because a database snapshot cannot make a collection of independent files/databases transactionally consistent.

Each successful bundle contains:

```text
<checkpoint-id>/
  home.tar       # uncompressed, regular-file-only, private data
  manifest.json  # version, owner, generation, archive checksum, per-file checksums
```

The returned receipt contains only `owner_id`, `generation`, `manifest_sha256`, and `file_count`. All file contents and path metadata are private; the manifest is not safe for public logs. Bundles are **not encrypted** by this prototype. Directories use mode 0700 and files 0600. Production storage needs its separately reviewed private/encrypted transport and key-access policy before real data can be used.

Restore requires the expected owner, exact generation, and manifest SHA-256 from a trusted controller record. Reading these values from the bundle itself would remove the ownership/integrity check. Hashes detect tampering only while that external reference remains trusted; they are not authentication by themselves. The utility rejects mismatches, corruption, missing/extra/duplicate members, symlinks, special files, unsafe paths, and existing destinations. It verifies into a private sibling staging directory before atomically renaming it. A local publish lock serializes cooperating publishers; it is not a distributed lease or an adversarial filesystem sandbox.

Limits are deliberately small for the fixture: 1,024 files/pending directory entries, 64 MiB aggregate payload, 1 MiB manifest, a bounded uncompressed archive, and a cooperative 20-second processing deadline. These limits are not a measured production browser-profile size. Slow filesystem calls are not subject to a hard preemptive wall-clock deadline. No compression, extraction shell command, cloud client, subprocess, or network call is used.

Excluded volatile entries: names `SingletonLock`, `SingletonCookie`, `SingletonSocket`, `DevToolsActivePort`, `LOCK`; suffixes `.pid`, `.sock`, `.socket`, `.lock`, `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal`. Nonvolatile symlinks/special files fail export. This is an explicit fixture exclusion policy, not a complete inventory of all upstream runtime artifacts. The live inventory must review any legitimate durable file matching these patterns.

## Cloudflare persistence choices

| Choice | Supported primitive | Remaining integration / tradeoff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default scheduling + immutable R2 checkpoints | Normal ephemeral root filesystem; export SQLite through its backup API and copy quiescent files into immutable private objects | Supports the `basic` gateway sizing option. Needs export/upload/commit/restore hooks, lifecycle control, owner checks, credential checkpoint handling, and application-consistent checkpoints. Last completed checkpoint defines recovery, not the last local write. |
| `durable_object` scheduling + native filesystem snapshots | `snapshotContainer()` captures the writable root filesystem; store its handle in DO storage and restore on start | Public beta; direct Container API required, not the `Container` SDK class. No `basic`; snapshots are image-version-bound, expire after 30 days without restoration, and exclude memory/processes/separate mounts. Still needs quiescence, owner/grant fencing, checkpoint selection and recovery tests. |
| Live SQLite on an R2 FUSE mount | Object-storage access through FUSE | Not selected: Cloudflare explicitly says FUSE lacks full POSIX semantics. It is not evidence that Hermes SQLite WAL/locking or browser databases are safe on that mount. |

Sources: [Cloudflare filesystem lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/faq/#is-disk-persistent-what-happens-to-my-disk-when-my-container-sleeps), [snapshot behavior](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/guides/snapshots/), [API exclusions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/api/durable-object-container/#snapshotcontainer), [scheduling policy](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/configuration/scheduling-policy/), [R2 FUSE limitations](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/examples/r2-fuse-mount/).

This prototype establishes a file-bundle format usable by an R2 adapter; it does not choose or implement either cloud option. Both require paid Containers. Native snapshots are not continuous durable storage, and their documented semantics do not prove application-consistent SQLite/browser recovery.

## Three-owner runtime boundary

The trusted Slack ingress resolves verified workspace/user identifiers to owner IDs. Up to three isolated full Hermes runtimes can be leased simultaneously. Each receives only its owner's home, browser state, workspace files, and authorized credentials. A shared Slack channel does not authorize access to another owner's checkpoint.
